name: AEGIS (AEGIS-128x2 / AEGIS-128x4)
workload: AEAD encryption/decryption throughput at 64 KB messages on Apple M5 Max, vs OpenSSL's AES-128-GCM backend
claimed_speedup: AEGIS-128x2 AEAD encryption 211.8 Gbps vs OpenSSL AES-128-GCM 70.8 Gbps at 64KB on M5 Max (~3x, derived from page data)
tradeoffs: Requires AES-NI/VAES/AVX-512 (x86) or ARM crypto extensions for peak throughput; unlike HiAE/ROCCA-S, AEGIS decrypts as fast as it encrypts (no AES-round latency in its keystream path)
caveats: AEGIS is already catalogued (KNOWN_LIST: github.com/aegis-aead/libaegis and github.com/aegis-aead/aegis-bitsliced). Included only as new tier-A evidence from hiae-aead/benchmarks, a reproducible harness with stated compiler/flags/CPU/OpenSSL version. Independently corroborated by mumble-voip/crypto-benchmark (tier B, GitHub Actions, 2024 snapshot): libsodium's AEGIS-128L at 0.647s vs OpenSSL AES-256-GCM at 2.525s for 1M x 4096-byte iterations (~3.9x), and vs OpenSSL ChaCha20-Poly1305 at 4.273s (~6.6x).
found_via: GitHub: search 'AEAD in:readme benchmark AES-NI' -> hiae-aead/benchmarks

name: HiAE
workload: AEAD encryption/decryption throughput at 64 KB messages on Apple M5 Max and AMD Zen 4, vs OpenSSL's AES-128-GCM backend
claimed_speedup: HiAE AEAD encryption 266.7 Gbps vs OpenSSL AES-128-GCM 70.8 Gbps at 64KB on M5 Max (~3.8x, derived from page data); 268.4 Gbps on Zen 4
hardware: Apple Silicon M5 Max (macOS 26); AMD Ryzen 7 7700 (Zen 4) at fixed 3.8GHz
tradeoffs: Decryption is up to 1.9x slower than encryption at 64KB (Zen4: 139.1 vs 268.4 Gbps) because the AES-round-then-fold state update recovers the message block only after the AES round finishes; multi-lane HiAEx2/HiAEx4 narrow this gap but need AVX-512+VAES on x86 or fall back to a much slower portable path
caveats: HiAE is already catalogued (KNOWN_LIST: github.com/concyclics/hiae). Included only as new tier-A evidence from hiae-aead/benchmarks. GitHub's license API returns 404 for concyclics/hiae (no detected LICENSE file), so usability is recorded as 'reference' for this specific repo even though a newer, MIT-licensed copy of the same algorithm exists at github.com/hiae-aead/libhiae (not filed as a separate entry since it is the same project/algorithm, just a different org).
found_via: GitHub: search 'AEAD in:readme benchmark AES-NI' -> hiae-aead/benchmarks

name: HiAE
workload: AEAD encryption/decryption throughput at 64KB messages, 4096-byte-aligned buffers, key/nonce setup included
claimed_speedup: HiAE AEAD encryption 266.7 Gbps vs AES-128-GCM 70.8 Gbps (~3.8x) at 64KB on Apple Silicon M5 Max (Apple clang 21.0.0, OpenSSL 3.6.4); 268.4 Gbps AEAD encryption on AMD Ryzen 7 7700 'Zen 4' (clang 21.1.8, -O3 -march=native, OpenSSL 3.5.5)
hardware: Apple Silicon M5 Max, macOS 26; AMD Ryzen 7 7700 'Zen 4' fixed at 3.8GHz, performance governor, turbo/frequency-scaling disabled
tradeoffs: Decryption up to ~1.93x slower than encryption on Zen4 (message block only recoverable after an AES round, same asymmetry class as Rocca-S); multi-lane HiAEx2/HiAEx4 variants trade some single-stream throughput for AVX-512/VAES parallelism
caveats: This is a Tier A independent benchmark (compiler, flags and CPU model all stated, code public) for a project already on the excluded/known list (concyclics/hiae); reported here as supplementary evidence per the is_evidence_for_known exception rather than as a new catalog entry. GitHub detects no license file for concyclics/hiae, so usability is recorded as reference pending confirmation
